reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer (packet-only: competency text + rendered samples, no generator source), 2026-07-27 re-review batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: A shape is divided into 2 equal parts. 1 part is shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?
A shape is divided into 2 equal parts. 1 part is shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?
A shape is divided into 4 equal parts. 1 part is shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?
A shape is divided into 4 equal parts. 1 part is shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?
A shape is divided into 2 equal parts. 1 part is shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Both target fractions are named correctly, with seeds 42, 43 and 46 keying 1/2 for two equal parts and seeds 44 and 45 keying 1/4 for four equal parts. The weakness is that the verb is 'Illustrate', while the stem 'A shape is divided into 4 equal parts. 1 part is shaded.' hands the child both the numerator and the denominator in words, so the answer can be transcribed straight out of the stem without any part-whole reasoning.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both halves and fourths are present, which covers the two fractions named. Not generated are the reverse direction, 'Which picture shows 1/4 shaded', the non-example check that parts must be equal, the whole-to-parts direction of dividing a shape yourself, and the set model of halving a group of objects, all of which 'as parts of a whole' fairly implies.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The stems themselves are two short declaratives plus a question, well matched to Grade 1 Quarter 4. The distractors are the problem: '3/8' at seeds 44 and 45 requires reading eighths, and '2/1' at seeds 42, 43 and 46 is an improper fraction denoting a quantity greater than one whole. Neither notation exists in a Grade 1 pupil's vocabulary at this point, so the option set demands symbols the node has not taught.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: One template carries the entire node with only the denominator changing, and seeds 42, 43 and 46 emit the byte-identical stem 'A shape is divided into 2 equal parts. 1 part is shaded.' so three of five draws are the same question. No shape is ever named, so circles, rectangles and squares are indistinguishable in the rendered text, and no partitioning or shading-the-model variation appears.

competency_alignment.rationale: The 1/2 items and the 1/4 items are structurally identical and differ only in a single numeral, so nothing in the sequence builds from the easier halving idea toward the harder fourth. A sound progression would move from equal-parts recognition, to naming the unit fraction, to constructing the illustration, and only the middle rung is present.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The denominators generated are exactly 2 and 4, matching the competency's explicit statement of 1/2 and 1/4 with no drift into thirds, fifths or sixths in the keyed answers, and every numerator is 1 as the unit-fraction framing requires. No quantity in any stem falls outside the whole being partitioned.
